_comment: Hand-compiled site facts with per-fact sources (research pass 2026-08-19). Coordinates for T-Ports/closed sites are TOWN-level (Nominatim/OSM); operator API provides facility-level for Bunge sites. capacity_t values: only where published. Commodity codes: WH wheat, BA barley, CA canola, LE lentils, FB faba beans.

port_capacities._source: ACCC Final Determinations Port Lincoln & Thevenard, 20 Jul 2021, Table 3.1 (https://www.accc.gov.au/system/files/Viterra%20Final%20Determinations%20for%20Port%20Lincoln%20and%20Thevenard.pdf); T-Ports: https://tports.com/lucky-bay/ + ACCC ibid.

extra_sites.name: Lucky Bay (T-Ports port)
extra_sites.coord_source: Nominatim/OSM 'Lucky Bay, South Australia' hamlet node (facility adjoins hamlet)
extra_sites.capacity_source: https://tports.com/lucky-bay/ (24,000 t port silos + 360,000 t bunkers 2 km away); ACCC 2021 Table 3.1 confirms 384,000 t
extra_sites.notes: Transshipment port opened 2019; no berth for ocean vessels - TSV MV Lucky Eyre shuttles to anchorage

extra_sites.name: Lock (T-Ports bunker)
extra_sites.coord_source: Nominatim/OSM town node; exact pad unpublished
extra_sites.capacity_source: https://tports.com/lucky-bay/ ('Lock bunker site: 140,000 tonnes in six bunkers')
extra_sites.notes: 'Site closed for 25/26 season' per tports.com/harvest; operated prior seasons from 2019. Read live 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-31, and confirmed IN SEASON on the Internet Archive snapshot of 14 January 2026 (mid-harvest), where Lucky Bay and Wallaroo carry 'By Appt.' hours and live segregations while Lock and Kimba carry the closure line and none.

extra_sites.name: Kimba (T-Ports bunker)
extra_sites.coord_source: Nominatim/OSM town node; facility 'east of Kimba township' per Grain Central
extra_sites.capacity_source: https://tports.com/lucky-bay/ ('Kimba bunker site: 150,000 tonnes in four bunkers')
extra_sites.notes: Built for 2021 harvest; 'Site closed for 25/26 season' per tports.com/harvest, on the same line the page carries for Lock (verified 2026-08-31). Confirmed IN SEASON on the Internet Archive snapshot of 14 January 2026 (mid-harvest) - the closure is not an off-season page state. Until 2026-08-31 this entry carried the closed_2025_26_season status with NO closure evidence recorded - only Lock's quote had been transcribed - while every 2025/26 finding in docs/r0_choice_geometry.md depended on both bunkers being closed.

extra_sites.name: Minnipa (closed)
extra_sites.sources_note: Stock Journal 6202314 is the original report; 6202864 is the companion EP story carrying the six-site list; the Farm Online URL is the syndicated reprint of 6202314 and was, until 2026-08-31, the only citation on five of these six entries. Cached at data/raw/press/stockjournal_6202314_17-silo-closures_20260831.html, data/raw/press/stockjournal_6202864_upper-ep-silos_20260831.html and data/raw/press/farmonline_6204914_17-silo-closures_20260831.html.
extra_sites.notes: Named closed in Viterra's June 2019 rationalisation of 17 up-country sites, six of them on EP. Primary source: Alisha Fogden, 'SILO SLASH: 17 Viterra grain sites to close', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 (upd. 7 Jun 2019), and 'Croppers angry as upper EP silos take a hit', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 - 'The sites of Minnipa, Kyancutta, Cungena, Waddikee, Kielpa and Wharminda have been closed.' The Farm Online item is the 7 Jun 2019 syndication of the first ('This story first appeared on Stock Journal') and is listed as a reprint, not as an independent outlet. Viterra's stated reasons, per operations manager Michael Hill: average truck size up 30 per cent since 2010 with bigger trucks going to bigger sites; quality-management and food-safety requirements; the closed sites were 'less than 2pc of total receivals (based on a five-year average)'. One of only TWO of the six that were operating the year before: 'six sites open last year at Minnipa, Kyancutta, Brinkworth, Paskeville, Millicent and Walpeup in Vic would not play a future role in the Viterra network'. NO PUBLISHED SOURCE ATTRIBUTES THE 2019 CLOSURES TO THE MAY 2019 EP RAIL SHUTDOWN. Neither Stock Journal story gives rail as a cause; 'freight redirection' survives only in a URL slug and appears nowhere in either body. Rail is mentioned once across both stories, by Minnipa cropper Matt Cook, about a different and earlier local closure. Any rail link is this project's inference and must be labelled as one. (Corrected 2026-08-31: this note previously read 'Closed in Viterra's 2019 network rationalisation after EP rail shutdown'. The trailing clause was unsourced and is withdrawn.)

NOT operating the year before: it is in the group of 11 'that were not open the year prior' that 'would also be closed permanently'. A pre-2019 network state that counts it as open overstates the 2018/19 network. NO PUBLISHED SOURCE ATTRIBUTES THE 2019 CLOSURES TO THE MAY 2019 EP RAIL SHUTDOWN. Rail is mentioned once across both stories, by Minnipa cropper Matt Cook, about a different and earlier local closure. Any rail link is this project's inference and must be labelled as one. CONTRADICTED, AND THE CONTRADICTION IS UNRESOLVED: Viterra's own weekly harvest report for the week ending 13 Nov 2022 names Cungena among sites that 'received their first new season deliveries'. Both sources are published and neither is retracted. What they jointly support is that it was closed in June 2019 and described as permanent, that it nonetheless took first new-season deliveries in 2022/23, and that no published evidence has it operating in any other season. The bare 'closed permanently 2019' tag this note used to carry is wrong as written; the defensible statement is a season range. See data/SOURCES.md 'cungena-status-contradiction'. Corrected 2026-08-31.
